title: MambaSL: Exploring Single-Layer Mamba for Time Series Classification
claim: Time-invariant parameters impose a fixed update rate and independent channels; time-varying ones adapt pacing and enable input-dependent mixing.
layout: 4 panels, left-to-right, TI vs TV pairs for two parameters
description: Four side-by-side panels with serif titles: TI-Δ, TV-Δ, TI-B, TV-B. The left two panels each show two time series, one red and one blue, as dotted-line plots over a time axis with ticks 0 to 4. In TI-Δ the intervals between ticks are uniform and labeled with a constant Δ. In TV-Δ the intervals are uneven and labeled Δ1 to Δ4, so each series gets its own pacing. The right two panels use small stacked colored blocks. TI-B shows fixed matrices B¹ and B² in gray, each multiplied with a green or purple input block. TV-B shows a weight matrix W_B producing an input-dependent B_t, which is then applied to the inputs. Curly braces show the combining step. Red/blue marks the series, and green/purple marks the channels.
caption: TI/TV parameterization of (left) $\Delta$ and (right) $\mB$ in the SSM. TI-$\Delta$ fixes the update rate, while TV-$\Delta$ adapts it to align sequences with varying speeds. TI-$\mB$ preserves channel independence, whereas TV-$\mB$ introduces input-dependent mixing. $\mC$ follows the same pattern as $\mB$ at the output stage, highlighting the temporal pacing of $\Delta$ versus the spatial routing of $\mB$ and $\mC$.
abstract: Despite recent advances in state space models (SSMs) such as Mamba across various sequence domains, research on their standalone capacity for time series classification (TSC) has remained limited. We propose MambaSL, a framework that minimally redesigns the selective SSM and projection layers of a single-layer Mamba, guided by four TSC-specific hypotheses. To address benchmarking limitations -- restricted configurations, partial University of East Anglia (UEA) dataset coverage, and insufficiently reproducible setups -- we re-evaluate 20 strong baselines across all 30 UEA datasets under a unified protocol. As a result, MambaSL achieves state-of-the-art performance with statistically significant average improvements, while ensuring reproducibility via public checkpoints for all evaluated models. Together with visualizations, these results demonstrate the potential of Mamba-based architectures as a TSC backbone.
